The record shows a run of dated moves: the Addition acquisition in July 2025, a first Global Chief Brand Officer in September 2025, the Levi's digital experience brief in December 2025 and the BRDNA Sequence and Sequencer launches in September 2026. The positioning line, "Independent creative innovation firm that builds AI-era 'intelligent brand systems' to keep client businesses ahead," decodes to a brand and design shop that now sells the rules and tools that let AI agents and ad systems produce on brand output, rather than producing the output itself. The record holds no headline claim; its prominence signals are multiple Campaign US shortlists in January 2026 and 23+ LinkedIn company ads pitching intelligent brand systems to tech brands.

The services list is intelligent brand systems, brand strategy and identity, digital experience design, campaigns and AI brand systems. Proprietary lines: BRDNA Sequence, an AI system teaching coding agents to build on brand; BRDNA Sequencer, a hyper personalized ad tool; and FutureVision, a roundtable series. No partner is listed; the site runs on Next.js.

Its AI posture is the whole positioning: BRDNA tools teach coding agents and ad systems to stay on brand, and it bought the AI design studio Addition; no AI search or visibility line shows (P1 absent).

Moves in date order: July 2025, acquired Addition; September 2025, hired Ren Rigby as first Global Chief Brand Officer and named Giacomo Groff general manager of the São Paulo office; December 2025, won the brief to redesign Levi's digital experience; January 2026, expanded its global Google leadership team for AI powered work; February 2026, launched a winter campaign for Arc'teryx Japan; September 2026, launched BRDNA Sequence and, per Fast Company coverage, the BRDNA Sequencer. The record lists no news list, no case study, no job posting and no pricing model. Conspicuously absent for a firm selling brand systems to be consumed by machines: any feed, schema or entity line (P2 absent), any measurement line, a headquarters and a headcount.

openings:
The strongest opening is the gap between the line it leads with and the work it can show: intelligent brand systems and the BRDNA tools carry the whole read, yet no case study, client or outcome on record describes them in use, and the two observed engagements are a website redesign and a winter campaign. A rival that can show a deployed brand system, with agents producing on brand output for a named client, is likely to win the enterprise technology buyer comparing the two (moderate confidence, since the launches are dated September 2026 and cases may follow). The falsifier: a BRDNA case study naming a client at the next compile.

Second, the shopping book: Google sits on six other tracked books and Levi's on two, and the instrument book holds both, so neither account is exclusive and both are contestable on described work.

Third, the machine readable layer: it sells systems for coding agents and ad systems while showing no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent), no llms.txt and no measurement line, so a rival that pairs brand systems with the entity and feed layer answer engines consume very likely holds the more complete offer. On price the record lists no model (P5 unknown), so an outcome priced offer meets no public answer; displacement reads 41.3, so a rate attack alone is unlikely to move an enterprise buyer, but the observed hubs in Argentina, Brazil and Indonesia give an onshore delivery pitch something concrete to point at.
